name: Trap System
description: A hidden hazard with a three-state lifecycle: undetected, detected, resolved (disarmed or triggered). world.hazard_volume owns the damage once a trap fires — a trap is not a second damage system, it is a visibility and agency layer over one. Detection keys off a perception check (progression.attribute_sheet answers those), disarm is a check with failure consequences, and a triggered trap delegates the hurt to the volume it wraps. Owning only the lifecycle keeps the trap honest in every view: an isometric crawler and a first-person grid-stepper render it differently but run the same three states.

inputs.name: detectionRadius
inputs.description: Tiles within which a passive detection check can reveal the trap. Two means the party sees the trap just before the point of no return — tension without cheapness.

inputs.name: disarmDifficulty
inputs.description: Default check difficulty to disarm. Per-trap data overrides this; the default exists so a designer can drop a generic dart trap without a stat block.

inputs.name: failureTriggersTrap
inputs.description: Whether a botched disarm sets the trap off. True makes disarming a gamble; false makes it free retries, which teaches players to disarm everything forever.

inputs.name: rearmable
inputs.description: Whether a disarmed trap can be reset by the player and used against enemies. Delightful in the right game; off by default because it doubles the test matrix.

outputs.name: trapStates
outputs.description: Per-trap lifecycle state: undetected | detected | disarmed | triggered.
